text.p: Mobutu Sese Seko, the ailing former leader of Zaire, left the Avicenne hospital in Rabat on Monday evening after undergoing urgent surgery at the weekend, a medical source said.

"President Mobutu, whose health has slightly improved, left Avicenne hospital this evening for an unknown destination...But he apparently needs intensive medical care later which necessitates his hospitalisation abroad," a Moroccan doctor, who declined to be named, told Reuters.
The doctor suggested that Mobutu might go to France for further treatment, but gave no details.
Communication (information) ministry officials were not immediately available for comment.

The 66-year-old former Zaire leader, who has been suffering from prostate cancer, was brought to the Moroccan capital from the northern town of Tangier on Friday and admitted to Avicenne's cardiology ward.
Morocco's official news agency MAP said earlier that he had suffered "serious bleeding complications" and underwent "radiological vascular intervention" on Saturday morning.
"The operation passed in good conditions and the patient was well," the agency said, quoting an authorised medical source.
Security forces and the royal guard were withdrawn from the cardiology unit on Monday evening and the public were allowed back into the area.
Mobutu, his family and entourage had been staying at a hotel south of Rabat, near King Hassan's palace at Skhirat, since their arrival in Morocco last month.
But on June 18 they moved to Le Mirage hotel at Cap Spartel, about 20 km (12 miles) from Tangier.
Officials had said they expected Mobutu to spend up to six weeks there. Diplomats said he had asked for political asylum in Spain and Portugal but had received no response.
A manager at Le Mirage confirmed on Monday that Mobutu's entourage was still at the hotel but declined to confirm whether the former president and his family were still there.
